title: Zoos and Wildlife Parks
objective: After this level you can explain what modern zoos try to do.
summary: The Arabian oryx returned from zoo and royal herds to reach Vulnerable in 2011. AZA sees zoos as conservation centers; Born Free argues such successes are rare.

cards.headline: The Arabian oryx vanished from the wild in 1972. Zoo herds brought it back.
cards.body: The last wild one is believed to have been shot in Oman. Ten years later, oryx were running free there again. It's one of the strongest cases for zoos, and it's also where the argument about zoos begins.

cards.headline: Nine oryx in Phoenix
cards.body: As the oryx disappeared, some of the last ones were captured to start a 'World Herd'. It began at the Phoenix Zoo with nine animals. With royal herds in Arabia, it supplied oryx for reintroduction: first in Oman in 1982, then in other countries. By 2011 about 1,000 lived wild, and IUCN moved the species to Vulnerable. No species once Extinct in the Wild had climbed three full categories before.

cards.headline: Two views of the modern zoo

items.label: AZA, the zoo association
points: Conservation is key to accredited zoos' mission

items.label: Born Free, an animal-welfare charity
points: Most zoo species aren't threatened in the wild
Very few zoo animals return to the wild

cards.headline: One success, read two ways
cards.body: The Association of Zoos and Aquariums counts conservation breeding, like the oryx herds, among zoos' core jobs. The Born Free Foundation argues that pointing to a handful of reintroductions risks suggesting there are many more, and that such cases can't justify keeping large numbers of animals that aren't threatened. One side sees a model; the other sees an exception.
